prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Reform UK’s 2024 “Contract with You” presents itself as a common-sense alternative to Conservatives and Labour, claiming Britain faces crises in immigration, public services, cost of living, and trust in politics. It pledges swift reforms in the first 100 days and beyond, arguing the state should work for the British people, protect culture and values, and deliver lower taxes, secure borders, and affordable energy.

Core pledges
- Freeze non-essential immigration; stop small boats by leaving the ECHR, detaining and deporting illegal arrivals, and returning boats to France.
- Zero NHS waiting lists while keeping care free at point of use; cut management waste; tax breaks for staff; use independent capacity.
- Make work pay by lifting the income tax threshold to £20,000 and raising higher rate to £70,000.
- Cut energy bills by scrapping Net Zero and levies; exploit UK oil and gas.

Immigration
- Freeze all but essential skills (mainly health). Offshore processing, no asylum from safe countries, no legal aid for non-citizens, immediate deportation of foreign criminals, restrict student dependents, 5-year residency to claim benefits. Employer Immigration Tax: higher NI (20%) on foreign workers (exempt health/care and very small firms).

Government waste and savings
- End Bank of England interest on QE reserves; mandate 5% efficiency across departments; cut red tape and halve foreign aid; improve HMRC collection.

Economy and business
- Personal: raise tax thresholds; cut fuel duty by 20p, scrap VAT and green levies on energy; big stamp duty cuts; restore VAT tourist shopping; IHT abolished below £2m, 20% above.
- Business: no corporation tax for profits under £100k; main rate to 20% then 15%; abolish IR35; VAT threshold to £150k; abolish business rates for high-street SMEs funded by a 4% online delivery tax; faster planning; deregulation.

NHS
- Zero basic rate income tax for NHS and social care staff for 3 years; end training caps; student fee write-offs tied to service; use independent/overseas capacity; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance; efficiency drives; public inquiry on excess deaths and vaccine harms.

Energy and Net Zero
- Scrap Net Zero and renewable subsidies; fast-track North Sea oil/gas and shale pilots; pursue SMRs and other technologies.

Law, order and justice
- 40,000 more frontline police; zero tolerance; more stop and search; tougher drug and knife penalties; scrap DEI roles; overhaul IOPC; expand prisons by 10,000 places; redefine hate crime; more courts and funding.

Education
- Patriotic, “balanced” curriculum; ban transgender ideology in schools; 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap interest on student loans; tougher free speech enforcement; more exclusions and PRUs; optional 2‑year degrees.

Benefits
- Stronger work requirements, in-person assessments, “two-strike” rule for job offers; focus on 16–34s.

Brexit and sovereignty
- Scrap retained EU laws; abandon Windsor Framework; avoid EU defence integration; prepare to renegotiate the TCA.

Defence
- Spend 2.5% of GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay rises; legal protections for troops; dedicated veterans department; recruit 30,000; procurement reform.

Housing
- Fast-track brownfield building; prioritize locals for social housing; restore mortgage interest relief for landlords; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; leasehold protections.

Families and culture
- Targeted marriage tax allowance (as finances allow); front-load child benefit; single-sex facilities; promote child-restricted smartphones; replace Equalities Act; comprehensive Free Speech Bill; reform BBC and scrap licence fee; national days for England and Wales; anti-corruption unit.

Transport and infrastructure
- Scrap HS2 remainder; ban ULEZ/LTNs and most 20mph zones; regional upgrades; mixed public/pension-fund utility ownership with caps on standing charges; single infrastructure funding stream.

Agriculture and fisheries
- Farm budget to £3bn; scrap climate-linked subsidies; protect country sports; restrict foreign access and supertrawlers; rebuild UK processing.

Pensions and social care
- Royal Commission on social care; stop offshore tax avoidance by providers; implement Mineworkers’ Pension reforms.

Funding summary (claims)
- Savings of c. £150bn per year plus £10bn from assumed extra growth; total costs c. £141bn per year.
